original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

scope_change_reason: The broad E6 non-star/T=4 windows and E6/E7 root-unit threshold evidence are active nearby. This fixes one new algebraic decoder family: a single rational bilinear form on the six-dimensional E6 root coordinates, with rank at most four. It tests a strict construction ansatz not covered by the standard-Gram table and gives a complete exact linear constraint system rather than an open-ended search.
object_and_question: For the 36 normalized E6 root lines with the fixed B0 pairing (B0_ts=1 on distinct orthogonal pairs), determine whether any rational 6x6 matrix L of rank at most four makes M_ts=x_t^T L x_s vanish on every ordered distinct orthogonal pair and remain nonzero on every diagonal entry, where x_t are exact root coordinates in a pinned basis.
changed_hypothesis: Restrict the decoder to M=R L R^T and rank_Q(L)<=4. This is narrower than an arbitrary rational four-total decoder. The favorable T=4 cost screen charges only the E6 per-total floor w=5, giving 20; E6 T=4 window thresholds are 21, 22 and 23. Forms with fewer than four totals are cheaper in this relaxation. Grant copies, frame changes, source access, restoration, hosting and precision for free. If a form survives, compute the exact F2 support-rank tariff before making any construction claim.
method_and_domain: Generate the complete E6 line set exactly from the E8 D8 and half-sign root families, choose and pin six independent roots, express all 36 roots in Q^6, then row-reduce over Q the 540 ordered orthogonal-pair constraints on all 36 entries of L. Test the complete solution-space basis for rank and diagonal conditions. One bounded pivot is allowed only if the exact nullspace is not one-dimensional; no random rational sampling or general E6 decoder search.
predecessors_and_overlap: PR #1590 head 08e134b4a0c7f04869dae703f2a2e688e53c44f0 / research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas: Lemma A covers T<=2 and E6 T>=3 remains open; standard-Gram B0 decoder is cost 37.
PR #2111 head 98da76c2839ba38538b510420dec54546ccabf0 / research/three-total-decoders: T=3 reductions and lift question, not the T=4 coordinate-form family.

PR #2125 head d9eb80ac183bb4df185ca044fd65432b817333bb / research/char2-threshold: exact standard-Gram costs and broad threshold evidence; it explicitly leaves E6 windows open and does not classify this L-family.
Discussion #1166 comment DC_kwDOU-508s4BIOSd: unclaimed E6 non-star and T=4 handoff; this claim narrows that handoff to a distinct rational coordinate-form family.
expected_evidence: A standard-library exact verifier with the root-coordinate and constraint hashes, rational row-reduction result, rank and diagonal certificates, Gram positive control, and semantic negative controls. If a rank<=4 form survives, include its exact support decomposition and fully charged B0 F2 block profile; otherwise state only the scoped family obstruction. No selected-record or kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop after exact elimination and one bounded structural pivot if needed. This replay found a one-dimensional kernel, so no pivot is needed. Do not promote the result to an obstruction for unrestricted E6 decoders.
actual_scope: Classify the full rational linear space of E6 B0 exact decoders that factor through the six-dimensional root-coordinate map, then test whether any member has at most four rational totals.
bottleneck_link: The open E6 T=4 root-unit windows require costs 21-23. A root-coordinate form with rank at most four would have an ideal floor-only bill at most 20, so excluding this family removes one plausible low-total mechanism while leaving arbitrary decoders open.
evidence: Exact standard-library replay: 36 E6 lines, 540 ordered orthogonal-pair equations, rational constraint rank 35, one-dimensional kernel generated by the rank-six Gram form; positive Gram controls and zero/mutant negative controls pass.

open_questions.question: Can an E6 T=4 decoder outside the image of the six-dimensional root-coordinate map meet one of the 21-23 cost windows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact kernel result rules out only a natural four-total coordinate-form family; other rational support vectors could still improve the E6 window.
open_questions.first_step: Specify a new support alphabet outside the root-coordinate image and compute its optimistic B0 F2 tariff before any synthesis.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package imposes p_j and q_j in the root-coordinate image and does not classify arbitrary rational decoder factors.
